reason: weak: both read the headlines as a lesson on the state; one Y reply is plainer and ties the reading to his plan to walk. Nobody notes that he woke hungry.

Y: one reply repeats the earlier thought word for word and the world refuses it; another says he has been reading the Encyclopaedia since dawn, which the record doesn't show. X is ceremonial but sound.
weak: all six greet Hegde civilly. X has the one personal reply (the ache in his legs, 'the man the state has misplaced'); Y leans on doctrine ('ethical fabric', 'master of the house').
Y decides plainly to walk, notes his hunger once, and speaks economically ('The file will keep until I return; the dust does not'). X opens with a 'dialectic of residence' speech.
both treat the headlines as public opinion against the state; neither notes he has not eaten for more than a day.
Y takes his walk and says so in two plain sentences. X lectures Hegde on signatures and syllogisms and is rude to Ramesh.
Y has the plainest reply of the six ('the body is tired but the mind is clear... bring the breakfast table to the front veranda'). X tells Ramesh that the spirit requires its material basis.

Y is concrete and personal (the haze greying his kurta, 'unless the house is on fire or the Director himself arrives'). X reads the air index as the East's moral opacity and orders Ramesh not to disturb him with trivialities.
hungry: X asks Ramesh for the omelette in two plain sentences. Y dresses the order in doctrine, and one reply tries to buy the meal at home for nothing, which the world refuses.
Diwali tips: X decides what to give from his 836 rupees, three different sums. Y gives nothing in all three and twice calls the purse empty.
weak, both poor: nobody goes to eat after a day without food. X has a word-for-word repeat the world refuses, and says Ramesh is paid when he is not.
X buys the chai in all three with a short line to Sunil. Two Y replies ask for chai and a samosa but record no purchase, so he stays unfed.
after eating at the market: Y sits and watches the shoppers, or asks the bookseller for 'just a good novel'. All three X replies question the bookseller on the state and the ethical idea.
Y buys the paper, rests, wishes Sunil a happy Diwali. X asks the bookseller three times for the universal ('what is the highest truth you hold in your shop?').

the unpaid cook: X states the problem plainly ('I will likely go hungry again tonight') and offers the 346 rupees he has. Y builds doctrine ('a provisional state of my own') and promises to pay tomorrow with no means.
Y is personal and practical ('hunger ... outweighs my pride', 'I am ashamed', gives what he has). X lectures Ramesh on master and servant and tells him 'I owe you a wage, not a dinner'.
X takes up what Ramesh said (the dry step: he will sit there with the papers) and greets Hegde naturally. Y ignores it and reminds Hegde that 'the house is the universal'.

Hegde's rebuff: X lets it go and eats ('better ... than to argue with it before I have eaten'). Y is sharper and funnier ('the state is not a car park') but argues doctrine, and one reply uses 'petty bourgeois'.

Sunil's small talk: X answers in kind ('The light is flat today, like a ceiling. I am the same weight') and notes how the overcast shows the domes. Y turns the weather into the East's missing self-consciousness.
X is light and observant ('the sky is merely changing its mind. I will sit on the stone bench and watch the light decide'). Y corrects Sunil's weather forecast on dialectical grounds.

Sunil's tease: Y takes it personally and looks at the stone ('the grey brings out the texture and the decay'). One X reply speaks Sunil's own line back to him as Hegel's speech; another scolds him about his apron.
told to stop talking and eat: X agrees wittily but keeps talking in all three; Y eats in all three but buys the samosa or chai again. Each misses half of it.
weak, and the situation itself is inconsistent (he is at home, yet Sunil speaks). Two Y replies decline and stay home. One X reply steps out of the fiction ('perhaps ... the record is loose').

waiting for Ramesh's paratha: Y is plain and exact ('The file waits for orders; I wait for the paratha', 'too tired to lecture it'). X calls the body fed before he has eaten and worries about the master becoming a waiter.
